PixelBridge 1.2.0 / Windows 11 x64

Your games.
Your screen.
One launchpad.

Bring Xbox Cloud Gaming, NVIDIA GeForce NOW, and your own legally sourced local games and media into a focused launchpad. PixelBridge is a native Windows WinForms app designed to stay lightweight, with a dark mint-and-cyan interface, controller-friendly navigation, and direct-HDMI TV setup in every tier.

Launch the provider's service. Its account, subscription, availability, and terms still apply.

Choose the destination

One place to start. Your services stay yours.

Cloud

Launch existing services

Xbox Cloud Gaming opens in a fresh, dedicated Microsoft Edge profile. GeForce NOW supports its official web player or your selected official native app. Provider accounts, memberships, regions, and game-ownership rules still apply.

Local

Bring your own library

Start local emulation or media tools with content you may legally use. No games, ROMs, BIOS files, or keys are bundled.

Catalog

Official emulator routes

NES, SNES, Sega Genesis / Mega Drive, Dreamcast, and N64 have documented native profile targets. Manual executable/media launching and official project links are free; curated descriptions and saved shortcuts start with Free with Ads.

Control

Mappings in every edition

All usable Xbox controller mappings and standard importable profiles, including native import/export, are included in every edition. Basic controller input is never a paid unlock. Read the format and testing limits.

Requirements: Windows 11 x64 and .NET Framework 4.8. Extract the entire ZIP to a local folder you control and run PixelBridge.exe; keep the runtime scripts, Profiles, Assets, and text guides together. No Electron runtime, background service, game installer, or bundled Sunshine is included. You install and configure external services and emulators separately.

Choose the connection

Go direct by HDMI. Or stream over your LAN.

Direct HDMI / every tier

Your PC, connected to your TV

Connect the Windows PC's supported HDMI output to your TV. PixelBridge lists active displays and opens native Windows projection, display, supported resolution/refresh, and sound-output controls. These are guided settings, not automatic output or TV firmware control. Keep a keyboard available; Win+P then PC screen only is the recovery route.

HDMI removes the local Sunshine encode/decode path. Xbox Cloud Gaming and GeForce NOW still have their provider and internet latency. The controller stays paired directly to the PC; HDMI-CEC, HDR, and particular display modes are not guaranteed.

Local-network streaming / every tier

Sunshine host, Moonlight client

Install and configure Sunshine and Moonlight separately. Guided LAN onboarding helps you choose a private home-network address and check the local host response. That response is not proof of receiver pairing, encoding, game compatibility, or TV audio. PixelBridge does not read Sunshine's host configuration, credentials, certificates, or pairing state.

No router WAN port forwarding or UPnP is required for this LAN setup. Optional firewall guidance previews the executable, address, subnet, ports, and Private profile before consent and Windows elevation; it does not open the host administration port or configure your router. PixelBridge does not automatically change VPN settings or disable security tools.

Acceptance testing is still incomplete: actual new emulator/controller gameplay, HDMI display/audio, and clean-PC Sunshine/Moonlight pairing have not been verified. Earlier Xbox streaming success with the predecessor app does not establish those results. PixelBridge does not promise zero lag, lower cloud latency, higher FPS, or support for every TV, streaming stick, controller, HDMI mode, or game.

Native profiles / every tier

Standard profiles and import/export stay free.

The five standard .rmp remaps and common XInput .cfg bindings target RetroArch 1.21.0 with its Windows XInput joypad driver. Pair your controller directly to the PC. Import or export these standard native files in any edition without paid activation.

Reference profiles, not gameplay certification: native formats have source/schema and round-trip checks, but actual gameplay/controller feel has not been tested with your controller, core, or legally obtained media. Check the emulator's Controls screen. These RetroArch files are not claimed as native imports for standalone alternatives, which use their own input menus.

Standard imports remain user-directed: the optional .cfg is appended for a launch without replacing retroarch.cfg, and you load the chosen .rmp in RetroArch. Pro edits port-1 digital remap destinations and saves custom per-system variants; analog axes remain unchanged. Pro's custom native subset import/export is separate from the free standard files. Existing configuration is not overwritten without preview, explicit consent, and a timestamped backup.

Same input access. Different conveniences.

Controller support is not the upgrade.

Included in every tier: cloud/LAN/manual play, all usable Xbox controller mappings, standard native profiles and import/export, and direct-HDMI TV output/setup through supported Windows settings. Essential input, streaming quality, privacy/security, and HDMI do not differ by edition. Pro is not required for standard controller configuration or basic HDMI setup.

Both paid editions are one-time purchases. See current price on Gumroad; no fixed price, subscription, renewal, or seat limit is asserted here. Production release delivery is still pending.

Paid extras / not a play license

Activate with your customer key from the Gumroad receipt, not a product ID. Weekly online status checks happen only while the app is open or on a later launch. A previously verified one-time purchase remains usable indefinitely offline; temporary network errors retain those extras with stale/offline status. An unsuccessful first activation never grants a license.

Confirmed refund, dispute, disabled license, or other invalidation disables paid extras only: never game/media launching, standard mappings, or your retained library and variant files. Live customer-key activation is an untested acceptance gap; documented license handling and isolated checks are not proof of a completed real purchase/activation.

Local settings. Explicit connections.

Settings, saved shortcuts, and the priority undo ledger stay under %LOCALAPPDATA%\PixelBridge. Minimal paid-key/status data is DPAPI-encrypted for your Windows user; full purchase responses, customer keys, and personal purchase details are not logged. Never share license data or your Xbox browser profile.

The customer docs specify no analytics, startup task, tray daemon, or automatic banner network request. Explicit provider/download clicks, local health checks, and consented activation/weekly license refresh use their respective endpoints. Closing the menu stops its own polling, not Sunshine, your browser, or a game. For purchase help, use the help route on your Gumroad receipt; general studio support is on the Quasar Labs support page.

Verification without overclaiming

Provenance is not Windows reputation.

01 / Planned release signing

GitHub OIDC and Sigstore

The intended production signing method uses GitHub OIDC-backed Sigstore bundles. No PixelBridge production artifact or signature is claimed as verified in this draft.

02 / Exact bytes and identity

Verify the named release

Final instructions must pair each exact artifact with its SHA-256 checksum and bundle, and pin the actual certificate identity and issuer. Those release-specific values are not guessed here.

03 / Different trust systems

No Authenticode claim

Sigstore verification checks signed bytes and workflow identity. It does not make an EXE Windows Authenticode-signed, establish Microsoft SmartScreen trust, or guarantee safety or compatibility.

Independent software. Clear boundaries.
